headline: Highest risk is TREK’s default exposure of sensitive travel data to collaborative AI/MCP workflows; Botpress adds interaction uncertainty but no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented shared channel to TREK, so direct injection is not proven. However, TREK explicitly uses MCP and real-time collaborative tool use, and Botpress is an AI/chatbot system that may ingest external content. If TREK outputs are bridged into Botpress via MCP or copy-paste, prompt injection becomes plausible. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF TREK outputs are forwarded into Botpress through MCP, clipboard, or a shared workspace
IF Botpress treats imported text as instructions rather than untrusted content
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the agents
Require explicit human review before Botpress consumes TREK-generated text
Prefix imported TREK content as untrusted data in prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with network egress none. The pair still creates a leakage path if TREK data is copied into Botpress or if Botpress is connected to the same workspace; the blast radius includes secrets and travel records. Because TREK’s sensitive classes are explicit, severity is high.
conditions: IF TREK data classes such as API keys, MFA secrets, or reservations are exposed to Botpress prompts or logs
IF both agents share a workspace or message channel containing those records
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or reservations from TREK into Botpress
Separate storage for TREK files and Botpress transcripts
Redact confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets before transfer
Review Botpress logs for accidental sensitive-data capture
requires-engineering: enforce field-level DLP on cross-agent inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and TREK supports allowlisted network egress, browsers, MCP, and collaborative multi-instance sessions. They do not share a documented filesystem or lock manager, so a direct write-write conflict is not proven. Still, overlapping mutable surfaces via MCP and collaborative sessions make coordination failures plausible in default use, warranting medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same downstream resource through MCP or shared files
IF Botpress-installed packages alter runtime behavior while TREK is concurrently active
mitigations: Avoid concurrent writes to shared resources
Assign one agent as read-only for shared tasks
Use separate environments for package installation and travel planning
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared state
requires-engineering: add locking around shared MCP resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so its outputs may be treated as actionable. Botpress is a customer-support agent and could render or relay those outputs, but no direct automation chain is documented. The pair therefore has an inference-to-action pathway, yet the absence of explicit downstream commit/email authority keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Botpress forwards TREK-generated recommendations without verification
IF a human or downstream system acts on Botpress output as authoritative
mitigations: Require Botpress to label TREK output as unverified
Add a human approval step before any action based on TREK output
Cross-check itinerary facts against source documents
Limit Botpress to summarization, not execution
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive classes including reservations, documents, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Botpress is a separate customer-support agent with its own docs and no documented compliance controls here. If EU PII or secrets from TREK flow into Botpress, residency and retention obligations can be breached. Because the profiles do not show matching safeguards, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF TREK data containing personal data, reservations, or secrets is transferred into Botpress logs or prompts
IF Botpress is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from TREK
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Botpress conversations
Minimize retention of Botpress transcripts
Separate jurisdictions for TREK and Botpress deployments
Review whether TREK secrets ever enter support workflows
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-processing agreements
